before: Maybe you started playing that part so early, and it took over so completely, that "What do I believe?" or "What do I want?" has no clear answer of your own. They sound like such easy questions, too. Back then, asking might have gotten you in trouble, or laughed at. Or there was just no way to ask. That can make "love yourself" feel pretty empty (love what, when the part you've been playing doesn't feel real?).

guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
From Survival to Experimental Play

When childhood is organized around avoiding pain and preserving attachment, attention goes into reading danger, meeting other people’s expectations, and keeping the bond. There is much less room for the ordinary experiments that answer, “What do I like? What do I want to try? Who am I when nobody is grading me?”

Identity grows through trial and error: choosing clothes, hobbies, friends, ideas, and roles, then changing your mind. When curiosity or mistakes bring ridicule, punishment, or withdrawal of love, the performed self gets better at surviving while the less-practiced self remains blurry.

brief:
- when childhood is organized around avoiding pain and keeping the attachment (the bond with the people you depend on), your attention goes into reading danger, meeting other people's expectations, and keeping that bond
- that leaves much less room for the ordinary experiments that would tell you what you like, what you'd want to try, and who you are when nobody is grading you
- identity grows through trial and error: trying things on, from what you wear to the people, ideas and roles you take up, and then changing your mind
- when curiosity or mistakes got you ridiculed, punished or loved less, the performed self got better at surviving, while the self that didn't get practice stayed blurry
